name: Robert M. Hertzberg
title: Initiative Proponent, Proposition 37 (2026); former California Senate Majority Leader and Assembly Speaker
background: Hertzberg was born November 19, 1954, in Los Angeles and grew up in Benedict Canyon before his family moved to Palm Springs, where he attended Palm Springs High School. He graduated magna cum laude from the University of Redlands in 1976 with a degree in history and English, then earned his J.D. from UC Hastings College of the Law in 1979. After law school he worked as an associate at a Beverly Hills firm and later formed Hertzberg & Hertzberg with his father. (Source: Wikipedia, Bob Hertzberg.)

Hertzberg represented the 40th Assembly District from 1996 to 2002, winning election in 1996 with 72 percent of the primary vote and 59 percent in the general election, and was unanimously elected the 64th Speaker of the California State Assembly on April 13, 2000, serving through 2002. As Speaker he led the chamber through significant Democratic gains, co-created the CAPITOL Institute with then-Assemblymember Bill Leonard to train new legislators, and established the Speaker's Office of International Relations and Protocol; after the September 11 attacks he temporarily closed the Assembly and set up a bipartisan Legislative Task Force on Terrorism. Following his Assembly tenure, he was recruited to partner at Mayer Brown LLP by former U.S. Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor. In 2005 he ran for Mayor of Los Angeles, launching his campaign via the website ChangeLA.com and calling for breaking up the Los Angeles Unified School District; he placed third in the primary, behind James Hahn and Antonio Villaraigosa, and endorsed Villaraigosa. He also chaired California Forward (2009-2012) and co-founded, with billionaire Nicolas Berggruen, the Think Long Committee for California (2010), and served as a formal and informal advisor to Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger. (Source: Wikipedia, Bob Hertzberg.)

Hertzberg returned to elected office in the California State Senate, representing District 18 (later renumbered) from December 2014 to December 2022, winning his first election with roughly 63 percent of the primary vote and about 70 percent in the general, and winning re-election in 2018 with 78.1 percent, the highest margin of any state legislative race that year. He served as Senate Majority Leader from December 2018 through 2022. He is term-limited from any return to the Legislature and, after leaving the Senate, was named a senior fellow to the Mission Possible Partnership in early 2023, working on decarbonizing high-emission industries; he also ran unsuccessfully for the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors' third district seat in 2022, losing to Lindsey Horvath. (Source: Wikipedia, Bob Hertzberg.)

During his Senate tenure Hertzberg co-authored several notable bills. He was the lead author, with then-Assemblymember Rob Bonta, of SB 10 (2017-2018), which would have eliminated most use of cash bail statewide; it passed the Legislature and was signed by Governor Jerry Brown on August 28, 2018 (Chapter 244, Statutes of 2018), but its implementation was blocked before taking effect when opponents qualified a veto referendum, Proposition 25, which California voters rejected in November 2020 by roughly 56.4 percent to 43.6 percent. SB 10's elimination of money bail never went into effect and California's cash bail system remained in place. He also authored the Bolstering Online Transparency (BOT) Act, SB 1001 (2018), requiring disclosure of automated 'bot' social media accounts, which Wikipedia's summary states was signed October 1, 2018 and took effect July 1, 2019; I was unable to independently confirm SB 1001's chapter number through the Legislature's bill-status database, which timed out repeatedly during this research, so that detail rests on the Wikipedia summary alone. He was a co-lead author, with Senator Ben Allen, of SB 450 (2015-2016), the Voter's Choice Act authorizing counties to run elections by mailing ballots to all voters combined with vote centers, signed by Governor Brown on September 29, 2016 (Chapter 832, Statutes of 2016). And he was one of six co-lead authors, again with Senator Allen, of SB 54 (2021-2022), the California Plastic Pollution Prevention and Packaging Producer Responsibility Act, signed by Governor Gavin Newsom on June 30, 2022 (Chapter 75, Statutes of 2022). Wikipedia's summary also credits Hertzberg with partnering with Governor Newsom on SB 1137 (2022), the oil-well setback law; California Legislature bill-status records show SB 1137's lead authors were Senators Lena Gonzalez and Monique Limón, so I have not listed it as a bill Hertzberg authored, though he may have supported or co-authored it in a lesser capacity not captured in this research. (Sources: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 10, SB 450, and SB 54; Wikipedia, Bob Hertzberg, for the BOT Act and the SB 1137 characterization.)

In October 2025 Hertzberg filed and was cleared to circulate Proposition 37 for the November 2026 ballot, which would authorize the California Housing Finance Agency to sell up to $25 billion in revenue bonds to fund second-mortgage down payment assistance loans for middle-income buyers of newly built homes. He is quoted in the measure's official ballot argument describing his goal as targeting housing supply rather than demand: 'I wanted to create something that would support the building of, and therefore supply, more middle-class housing... The subsidies raise prices, but they don't add supply.' The measure's largest funders are Homeownership for Families, sponsored by the California Association of Realtors, and Building a Better California. (Source: content/measures/ca-prop-37-2026.json in this voter guide; California Secretary of State initiative-circulation notice.)
voting_record_highlights: SB 10 (2017-2018), eliminating most cash bail statewide: Hertzberg was lead author with then-Assemblymember Rob Bonta. Signed by Gov. Jerry Brown on August 28, 2018 as Chapter 244, Statutes of 2018, but its bail-reform provisions never took effect because California voters rejected a referendum on the law, Proposition 25, in November 2020 by about 56.4%-43.6%, repealing it before its effective date. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 10; Wikipedia, 2020 California Proposition 25.)

SB 450 (2015-2016), the Voter's Choice Act, authorizing counties to conduct elections by mailing ballots to all voters combined with vote centers: Hertzberg was a co-lead author with Sen. Ben Allen. Signed by Gov. Jerry Brown on September 29, 2016 as Chapter 832, Statutes of 2016. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 450.)

SB 54 (2021-2022), the California Plastic Pollution Prevention and Packaging Producer Responsibility Act: Hertzberg was one of six co-lead authors, with Sen. Ben Allen, Luz Rivas, Skinner, Stern, and Wiener. Signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom on June 30, 2022 as Chapter 75, Statutes of 2022. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 54.)

SB 1001 (2018), the Bolstering Online Transparency (BOT) Act, requiring disclosure of automated social-media 'bot' accounts: per Wikipedia's summary, Hertzberg authored this bill, which was signed October 1, 2018 and took effect July 1, 2019. I could not independently verify this bill's chapter number through the Legislature's bill-status database due to repeated fetch timeouts during this research, so this entry rests on the Wikipedia source alone rather than a primary legislative record.
